item.title: SGA Changes in Oracle 26ai - Subpools and Durations
item.description:
Oracle’s SGA memory pools have undergone regular changes over the years and across different versions. Oracle 26ai is no exception and introduces another redesign of SGA memory pools, such as the shared pool.

This first part of this post explains how Oracle 26ai changes the number of subpools and durations in various SGA memory pools compared to Oracle 19c, while the second part shows how to trace and observe them using low-level probes. For additional background information on this subject, refer to sources 1, 2, and 3.

item.title: Bypassing oradebug Restrictions
item.description:
In Oracle 26ai, the execution of certain oradebug commands and actions is no longer possible, as Oracle has changed the default value of the undocumented parameter _disable_oradebug_commands from none to restricted.

This change causes some oradebug functionality to stop working, as previously discussed by Jonathan Lewis in this blog post. Moreover, Mikhail Velikikh noted in a comment on the blog post that the parameter change from none to restricted was already introduced in RU 19.24.

item.title: UUID Generation In Oracle 26ai
item.description:
Some time ago, several bloggers wrote about the new support for UUIDs in Oracle 23ai/26ai (see the blog posts referenced in 1 and 2). This made me curious about how Oracle generates UUIDs behind the scenes and what exactly happens internally when a UUID is created. So, rather than discussing the pros and cons of UUIDs, this note provides a drill-down into Oracle’s UUID implementation details.

Oracle 23.7 introduced a new uuid() function, which generates 128-bit random UUIDv4 values compliant with RFC 9562. Historically, Oracle has provided the sys_guid() function, but the values it generates are predictable and not truly random.
